parts.text: A student investigates the period of a pendulum. Fig. 1.1 and Fig. 1.2 show the set-up. Fig. 1.1 Fig. 1.2

ms.label: 1(a)
ms.text: Clear use of horizontal aid OR bob touching rule

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student adjusts the length of the pendulum until the distance l , measured from the bottom of the clamp supporting the pendulum to the centre of the pendulum bob, is 50.0 cm. He displaces the bob slightly and releases it so that it swings. Fig. 1.2 shows one complete oscillation of the pendulum. He measures and records the time t for 20 complete oscillations.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate, and record in Table 1.1, the period T of the pendulum. The period is the time for one complete oscillation. [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate, and record in Table 1.1, the value of T 2 . [1] Table 1.1 l / cm t / s T / s T 2 / s 2 50.0 28.2 60.0 31.2 1.56 2.43 70.0 33.6 1.68 2.82 80.0 35.8 1.79 3.20 90.0 38.2 1.91 3.65 He repeats the procedure using l values of 60.0 cm, 70.0 cm, 80.0 cm and 90.0 cm. The readings and results are shown in Table 1.1.

ms.label: 1(b)(ii)
ms.text:
T = 1.99 (to 2 decimal places only, correctly rounded)
2

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of T 2 / s 2 ( y -axis) against l / cm ( x -axis). Start the T 2 / s 2 axis at a convenient value close to the minimum value of T 2 / s 2 . [4]

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
Axes of graph correctly labelled with quantity and unit and right way round
Suitable scales
All plots correct to ½ small square
Good line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ........................................................ [3]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
Triangle method clear on graph
Triangle at least half the length of the line between extreme plots used
G value in range 0.038 – 0.044

ms.label: 1(e)
ms.text: Reaction time / human error a smaller part of time measured
